clue.text: Academic type pulls up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, that is backwards

parts.note: pulls means tows, as a truck tows a car

explanation.surface: A studious type hauls something upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A swot is British slang for a student who studies very hard, an academic type.

clue.text: Volunteers in smart compound

indicators.note: in tells us the volunteers go inside the word for smart

parts.note: smart in the sense of upper-class or elegant is posh
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Volunteers are housed in a smart walled compound.
explanation.definitionFit: Potash is a potassium compound, such as potassium carbonate, used in fertiliser.

clue.text: Ann, a polite product of Italy

indicators.note: a product is something worked up from raw material, so the preceding letters are remade into a new order

explanation.surface: A courteous woman called Ann is something Italy has produced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'product' reworks ANN plus A POLITE into the answer. The definition is adjectival: belonging to Naples is one way of being of Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Neapolitan means belonging to Naples, a city in Italy, so it is an Italian adjective.

clue.text: Hero-worshipper lacking a ready source

indicators.note: lacking means the hero-worshipper is missing one letter, here the a

parts.note: in Greek myth Leander loved Hero and swam the Hellespont nightly to see her

explanation.surface: A fan of some hero is without the source of something ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hero-worshipper' looks like any fan, but it is Leander, lover of Hero. 'Ready' is British slang for cash (the readies), so a ready source is a moneylender.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready is slang for cash, and a lender is where you go to obtain money.

clue.text: Last song of reform in USSR?

definitions.text: Last song of reform in USSR?

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so the letters of the two words are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Perhaps the final tune heard as Soviet reforms took hold.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: the 'reform' of 'last song' gives the openness policy that reformed the Soviet Union and played out its last song.
explanation.definitionFit: Glasnost, meaning openness, was Gorbachev's reform policy in the 1980s USSR, shortly before the union ended.

clue.text: Dog, or feature thereof

definitions.meaning: to dog someone is to follow them closely, as a detective does
a part of a dog's body, the bit it wags

explanation.definitionFit: To tail is to follow secretly, like dogging, and a dog has a tail at its rear.

clue.text: Saintly bishop provides vehicle parking at college

indicators.note: at places the vehicle and parking after the college in the answer

parts.note: poly is short for polytechnic, a kind of British college
a car is a vehicle
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A holy bishop arranges for a car park at his college.
explanation.walkthrough: Saint Polycarp was a second-century bishop of Smyrna, martyred for his faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Polycarp was an early Christian bishop of Smyrna who was venerated as a saint and martyr.

clue.text: Traffic hazard could be sinister

definitions.meaning: a sharp curve in the road is a danger to drivers
in heraldry a ... sinister is a diagonal stripe on a shield

explanation.definitionFit: A curve in a road endangers traffic, and the heraldic stripe called a bend can be sinister.

clue.text: Bread should be sufficient

definitions.meaning: a loaf made from flour of the entire grain
read as two words, a complete repast ought to be enough to eat

explanation.definitionFit: Wholemeal is a type of bread, and split into two words it means an entire meal, which is filling.

clue.text: United, except a student who is single

indicators.note: except means leaving out, so one letter is taken from the phrase for united

parts.note: all one means united, everyone together as a single body
L, for learner, is the usual crossword student

explanation.surface: A single student is excluded from a united group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United' is the phrase ALL ONE; 'except' removes one L ('a student') from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being alone means being by oneself, unaccompanied, which is what single describes.

clue.text: Car parking for one without wheels

parts.note: a tram is a car running on rails, called a streetcar in America
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Somewhere to park the car of someone who has no transport.
explanation.walkthrough: A tramp is a vagrant who walks the roads on foot, hence someone without wheels.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramp is a homeless wanderer who travels on foot, having no vehicle at all.

clue.text: Shown to have perished without second drama

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the word for perished wraps the other pieces

parts.note: to have perished is to have died
S is the abbreviation for second, as in units of time
a drama is a play

explanation.surface: Proven to have died even without a second piece of theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking, so DIED surrounds S PLAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Displayed means put on view, which is what being shown amounts to.

clue.text: Carol's hard at work as a student

indicators.note: at work means busy and reworked, so the letters are put into a new arrangement

parts.note: carol's read as carols gives the letters of the songs
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A girl named Carol works hard as a student.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar is a learned person or a pupil, one who studies.

clue.text: Conveyors of fuel for fires

definitions.meaning: coal is carried in large bags
to fire someone is to dismiss them from a job

explanation.definitionFit: Coal travels in sacks, and an employer who sacks a worker fires them.

clue.text: Nothing bad having current for lighting

parts.note: O is nothing, the shape of zero
ill means bad, as in ill will
amp, short for ampere, is the unit of electric current

explanation.surface: Nothing wrong with having electric current for lights.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: the answer is something used for lighting.
explanation.definitionFit: An oil lamp burns paraffin to give light, so its use is for lighting a room.

clue.text: Bulletin broadcast about the Spanish with news of wreck

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the remade letters go round the Spanish article
to broadcast is to scatter, so the letters of the word are spread into a new order

parts.note: el is the Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A radio news report on Spain carries word of a shipwreck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' turns BULLETIN into LUTINEBL, which goes 'about' EL. The Lutine Bell hangs at Lloyd's of London, the insurance market, and was rung when news of a lost ship arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lutine Bell at Lloyd's of London was traditionally rung to announce the loss of an insured ship.

clue.text: Capital is below average

indicators.note: in a down clue, below puts the second piece underneath the first

parts.note: par means average, as in up to par

explanation.surface: Money is below the normal level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money but means a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Paris is the capital city of France.

clue.text: Split of Tory and Socialist

parts.note: C stands for Conservative, the party whose members are called Tories
the left is the socialist wing of politics

explanation.surface: A rift between the Conservative and Socialist parties.
explanation.definitionFit: A cleft is a split or fissure, as in a cleft in a rock.

clue.text: Demanding much of an old stager?

definitions.meaning: making heavy demands, strict and requiring great effort
split as ..., the performing of someone who used to be an actor

explanation.definitionFit: Exacting means requiring a lot, and broken up it is the former acting of a retired performer.

clue.text: 25 short of a large cask, brings back a small one

indicators.note: short of means the word for a cask is cut by its final letter

parts.note: a butt is a large cask for wine or beer

explanation.surface: A big barrel cut short gives back a little tub.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer to 25 is ONLY, which also means 'but'. There is a second wordplay: 'brings back a small one' reverses TUB, a small cask.
explanation.definitionFit: But can mean only, as in 'I have but one life', matching the cross-referenced answer.

clue.text: Spooner takes bed to remain — in the bum!

indicators.note: Spooner names the Reverend Spooner, who swapped the opening sounds of words

parts.note: the sack is slang for bed, as in hit the sack
to bide is to remain or wait

explanation.surface: Spooner goes to bed in order to stay, a kick in the backside.
explanation.walkthrough: SACK BIDE with S and B exchanged gives BACK SIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: Backside and bum are both informal words for the buttocks.

clue.text: One who records a spill

definitions.meaning: someone who makes recordings on tape
a spill is a thin strip of wood or paper used to light a fire or candle

explanation.definitionFit: A taper is a thin candle used to carry a flame, like a spill; and someone who tapes things.

clue.text: Can tins be a sort of tin cans?

indicators.note: be asks whether these letters can become something else, a sign that they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about whether tin cans can be rebranded as tins.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue asks whether 'Can tins' can 'be' rearranged into the answer; it can, as can 'tin cans'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stannic describes tin in its higher valency, as in stannic oxide, so it names a sort of tin compound.

clue.text: Are they no good in handling fries?

definitions.text: Are they no good in handling fries?

parts.words: Are they no good in handling fries?
parts.note: playful question about whether hands are useless for eating chips

explanation.definitionFit: Fingers are what we handle food with, and long thin chips are themselves called fingers.

clue.text: Name of retreating enemy

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the two words are read from end to start

explanation.surface: The name of a foe in retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: Foeman is an old-fashioned word for an enemy in war.

clue.text: There's space on the roster, so put my name down

indicators.note: in a down clue, on places the first piece above the second

parts.note: an en is a printer's space, half an em wide
a roster is a list of names

explanation.surface: There is room on the rota, so sign me up.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlist is to sign up, putting your name down for service or membership.

clue.text: English trousers may be turned up

indicators.note: may be suggests the letters could become something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: English trousers might have turn-ups.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' suggests trouser turn-ups, but describes a nose.
explanation.definitionFit: Retroussé, from French, describes a nose that is turned up at the tip.

clue.text: Wax is a heartless game

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the game is removed

parts.note: rugby is a game played with an oval ball

explanation.surface: Polish is a game without spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wax' looks like polish but is the surname of Ruby Wax, an American-born comedian well known on British television.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruby Wax is a comedian, so her first name partners the surname Wax in the clue.

clue.text: 19 across, nothing more

definitions.meaning: the answer to 19 across means merely, as in but a child

explanation.definitionFit: Only means merely or just, the same as the word but in 'but a moment'.

clue.text: Live with old cartoonist down under

parts.note: to live is to be, to exist
Sir David Low was a famous New Zealand-born political cartoonist of the twentieth century

explanation.surface: Living with a former cartoonist in Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down under' suggests Australia, and Low came from New Zealand, but here it simply means underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Below means underneath, lower down, the plain sense of down under.

clue.text: Drink in between partners

indicators.note: between means the little word sits inside the pair of partners

parts.note: West and East are partners at the bridge table

explanation.surface: A drink shared among companions.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge, West and East play as partners, giving W and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Wine is an alcoholic drink made from fermented grapes.

clue.text: To rusticate a student is commonplace

parts.note: to rusticate is to send a student down from university for a time, so to ban them
L, for learner, is the usual crossword student

explanation.surface: Sending a student down is a routine event.
explanation.walkthrough: Rusticate is Oxbridge slang for suspending a student from university.
explanation.definitionFit: Banal means trite and unoriginal, just what commonplace describes.

clue.text: Send daily hash, which is very wrong

indicators.note: to make a hash of something is to mess it up, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Sending out a daily mess is a grave error.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadly sin, like pride or greed, is a mortal wrong, gravely wicked.
